decisions.reason: As a low-risk extension of the core bread assortment with no visible negative feedback, it likely meets a satisficing aspiration level and is inexpensive to continue under current industry growth.
The premium raisin Christmas stollen clearly exceeds aspiration levels through its repeated gold medal and strengthens the firm's reputation in a core seasonal category.
This seeded rye mixed bread fits the firm's established capabilities and customer expectations, and with no sign of underperformance there is little reason for problemistic search away from it.

Although somewhat niche, the dark barley malt rye bread still builds directly on existing bread know-how and can be retained while its market acceptance remains uncertain because the firm likely has some slack.
A marzipan Christmas stollen is a close seasonal variant of the established confectionery offer, so maintaining it is a reasonable satisficing choice absent evidence of disappointing results.

The ancient grain bread uses the firm's traditional craft image and current consumer interest in heritage grains, so boundedly rational management would likely continue it unless clearer signs of failure emerged.
